- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to account for downward pressure.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a downward bias adjustment of 2–5% per day.  
- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., > 0.3) but forecast is flat or declining, increase forecast by 3–5% to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overfitting to recent highs; use 14-day rolling mean as a sanity check before finalizing forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), apply a mean-reversion bias toward 10–15% below recent peak.
